name: BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS), county-level
update_frequency: monthly, with an annual benchmark revision
license: US federal government data, public domain

correlation.note: Not computed. BLS itself canceled at least one recent month's release during a government shutdown (Oct 2025 per BLS/state labor-agency notices), which should be checked for recurrence before depending on monthly cadence.

recommendation_summary: The public v1 API needs no key (25 series/query, 25 queries/day, 10 years of history per request) and would be easy to wire up, and employment growth is a plausible Growth Score input. But county is the finest granularity BLS publishes for both LAUS and its establishment-level QCEW program (QCEW does not go to ZIP level, correcting an earlier pass of this memo) — and NYC's five counties are the five boroughs, so it can't distinguish neighborhoods within a borough at all. That's a much coarser signal than every other metric already in the Growth Score (NTA-level housing pipeline, transit, crime, ACS income/education); it would functionally be a single number repeated across dozens of NTAs per borough. A genuinely finer-grained employment proxy would have to come from a different source entirely, such as Census ZIP Code Business Patterns (ZBP) — establishment and employment counts by ZIP, from Census rather than BLS — which this research pass did not have search budget left to evaluate. Given the project is actively building out NTA-granularity signals, county-level LAUS on its own is a weak addition; worth reconsidering alongside ZBP or another sub-county source in a future pass.
